correctness.rationale: For n>=2 and p on boundary Σ|p_i|=1, coordinatewise absolute-value folding in coordinates 2..n is 1-Lipschitz and sign reflections fix v=e1; thus shortest path can be studied on union of two regular (n-1)-simplices with apices ±e1 and shared equatorial simplex Q. Unfolding their faces into a common Euclidean (n-1)-plane yields an exact straight segment; at p1=-t<0 its crossing point is q=c+(1-t)/(1+t)(u-c), a convex combination in Q. Height squared h²=n/(n-1) then yields d(v,p)²=||v-p||²+4t/(n-1), with no excess for p1>=0. Since ||v-p||²>=(1+t)²>=4t, maximum ratio √(n/(n-1)) occurs only t=1, p=-v. Surface-area-uniform points choose 2^n congruent simplicial facets and Dirichlet(1,...,1) coordinate magnitudes; hence positive excess tail P(Z>z)=1/2 (1-(n-1)z/4)^{n-1} on [0,4/(n-1)] and atom 1/2 at zero. Integrating beta moments gives E d²=(n+3)/(n+1)+2/[n(n-1)]. Degenerate equatorial and n=2 cases included.
